output.brief: The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, and since then the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. About 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts were affected. 34% of those had cancelled by 31 July, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Churn among Quillbook accounts is about 6% a month, whether or not they have the price lock. Accounts with no connector are flat at about 1.9%, in every seat band. The seat-band "dose-response" in the finance analysis is confounded, because Quillbook accounts have larger seat counts. The health panel counts only errors, and these failures are logged as warnings, so nobody saw them. Tallymarsh cancellations are too few to show an effect. How sure I am: fairly sure (roughly 85%). Next steps: make the Quillbook fix (move to v3, 3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority. Contact all Quillbook accounts, including those who cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. Do not roll back the price. Review the Tallymarsh log before committing a rebuild. Make the health panel count warnings.
